title: Recovery time and rotation thresholds for Nardostachys (study-matrix extrapolation)
question: Using only the study's own matrices, after how many years does abundance recover from one harvest, and what rest interval keeps the annualised growth rate >= 1 under repeated harvest?
hypothesis: Recovery lengthens with intensity; minimal rotation length increases with intensity; values will NOT match the paper's recovery times (5/17/33 yr) because COMPADRE stores 3-year mean matrices that already include post-harvest recovery.
method: recovery_time, periodic_lambda; sensitivity to control choice (outcrop control vs meadow)
finding: Recovery times are shorter than published (not reproduced) - a known limitation of mean matrices. Rotation thresholds are model extrapolations and depend on which control is used; shown in Simulate as 'study-matrix extrapolation', never as a permitted rotation.

result.paper_recommendation: <10% in outcrops, <25% in meadows, >=5 years between harvests
result.assumption: each harvest year reuses the 1999-2002 mean treatment matrix; control years reuse the control mean matrix; no density dependence or stochasticity
